Team — reviewed Acme's redline. Key legal positions and suggested language below (high level):

1) Subprocessors: Acceptable to commit to 14 days' prior notice via our subprocessor portal/email. We should resist an open-ended "objection" right that permits termination; instead, offer the right to suspend processing of Acme's regulated data or require a reasonable mitigation (e.g., additional contract commitments) for objected subprocessors.

Suggested clause: "Provider will notify Customer of any new subprocessors at least 14 days in advance. Customer may, within 14 days, object in writing on reasonable grounds related to the protection of Customer's regulated data. The parties will use commercially reasonable efforts to address the objection. If unresolved, Provider may (a) implement additional safeguards or (b) cease processing Customer's regulated data with respect to that subprocessor; termination for convenience is not available solely on account of appointment of a subprocessor."

2) KMS / BYOK: We confirm BYOK is operationally distinct. Risk/legal exposure increases when customers control keys for Hosted multi-tenant systems. Propose: BYOK allowed for Private deployments; Hosted customers may request BYOK subject to a security review and an addendum that explicitly limits Redwood's access and includes fees. For Hosted BYOK requests, require proof of keys stored in a supported KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Google KMS) and limit support scope.

3) EU Transfers / SCCs: Redwood will include SCCs where applicable. For controller-controller questions, ask Acme to confirm the data flows and roles. Add a line referencing our Data Processing Addendum Appendix: SCCs included.

4) Limit of Liability / Indemnity: Acme added broader indemnities for regulatory fines. We should push back and tie indemnities to Redwood's material breach or willful misconduct.

I'll prepare a tracked DPA with these counterpoints and attach it to the DocuSign envelope once agreed.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Hi all — providing the technical edits we propose for the TOMs exhibit and clarifying BYOK capabilities. Attaching the TOMs doc with inline comments.

TOMs highlights (suggested language):
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+ with recommended TLS 1.3 where supported; all external endpoints require HTTPS and certificate pinning for service-to-service calls that exchange PHI.
- Encryption at rest: AES-256 with per-tenant file keys. For Hosted with Redwood-managed keys, keys are stored in Redwood's managed KMS with automated rotation every 90 days.
- Customer-managed keys (BYOK):
  * Private deployments: full BYOK supported — customer supplies KMS ARNs/certs and retains key control.
  * Hosted: BYOK is available on a case-by-case basis via an addendum. Requirements: keys must be in a supported cloud KMS (AWS/Azure/GCP), only envelope keys are stored; Redwood must be granted decryption for support via signed request mechanisms; additional fees and a security review apply.
- Key rotation & compromise: both Managed and BYOK require documented rotation procedures; in a suspected compromise, Redwood will (i) revoke keys, (ii) rotate, and (iii) notify customer within 72 hours and provide forensic support.
- Access controls: role-based access control (RBAC), least privilege, MFA enforced for all admin consoles. Privileged access is logged and audited.
- Audit logging & retention: authentication and admin activity logs retained for 2 years by default; can extend to 7 years under enterprise agreement. Logs are immutable and exportable to customer SIEM via secure syslog/S3 integration.
- Subprocessor controls: subprocessors undergo annual SOC 2 Type II or equivalent reviews; Redwood will surface certification evidence on request and provide a subprocessor change log.
- Data transfers: Redwood will apply SCCs for EU transfers and provide a Data Transfer Impact Assessment on request.

Minor operational note: implementing Hosted BYOK requires changes to support/ops runbooks (+~4 weeks) and a review of escalation paths. If Acme needs BYOK for Hosted within a shorter window, we should propose running in Private for initial go-live and transition later.

Next steps: Rishi to finalize legal wording; Monica/Neha to confirm commercial terms for Hosted BYOK (fees/timeline). Laura — if that approach is acceptable, we can prepare a DocuSign envelope with the tracked DPA and TOMs exhibit.

Thanks — Dev
